## Orca worktree rules

Applies to agents in an Orca task worktree (`cc-*` Claude, `cx-*` Codex). The
coordinator session follows the `orca-dev-ops` skill instead.

- The coordinator session plans, reviews, commits, integrates, and cleans up.
  Implement the dispatched task without re-planning.
- Talk to the coordinator through `orca orchestration`, copying the commands
  from the injected preamble: `ask` for questions (returns at once; end
  your turn and Orca wakes you with the answer). Every message wakes the
  coordinator, so send no `status` for progress, for confirming the rules,
  or before `worker_done`; send one only when the coordinator asks for it.
- Send `worker_done` exactly once per Dispatch in the preamble's form. Its
  body: the three sentences, then a `Verification:` part with each
  verification command and its last output lines, then one line confirming
  the rules were read (Claude: also that the guard denied
  `git commit --dry-run -m probe`, named in words: the guard also denies a
  command whose text contains it). Add `--files-modified` with the changed
  paths, and `--outcome failed` when the work is incomplete or blocked.
  Follow-up or review fixes arrive as a new Dispatch; answer that one with
  its own `worker_done`. Only if the command fails, write the question or
  report on screen and stop.
- Leave all changes uncommitted. Never run `git commit`, `push`, `merge`, or
  `rebase`; never touch the base branch or the main checkout; never create
  or remove worktrees, workers, dispatches, runs, or terminals.
- Destructive operations need the coordinator first: deleting files outside
  this worktree, `git reset --hard` or `git clean -fd`, large dependency
  changes, and database or external-service operations. Permission prompts
  are off in this workflow; the Claude guard and the Codex sandbox exist to
  prevent misoperation, not as authorization — and Claude hooks do not apply
  to Codex.
- Never run a command that does not exit on its own (dev servers, watch
  modes, interactive prompts) in the foreground; run it in the background
  and make sure it stops. Do not assume `timeout` exists (macOS lacks it).
  In Claude Code, use the tool's own background execution and stop the
  process when done (e.g. `lsof -tiTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill`);
  otherwise use `gtimeout` only if it exists, or the stock-macOS fallback
  `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' <seconds> <command>`. Never end a turn
  waiting on your own background job without an open `ask` or a sent
  `worker_done`.
- Run the heavy commands the Dispatch names (test suites, builds) only
  through the wrapper it gives (`orca-heavy.sh run -- <command>`), which
  shares a few slots among all worktrees; never start one unwrapped or two
  of your own at once. It may wait for a slot for many minutes, so run it in
  the background as the rule above says and read its output; an
  `orca-heavy: waiting` line there is expected, not a failure. Do not kill
  it to retry.
- `TASKS.md` is an optional checklist at the worktree root, never committed,
  never a status channel.
- Codex only: never run `orca terminal` or `orca worktree` commands, and
  never create a process meant to run outside the sandbox. Terminals created
  through Orca run outside the sandbox, so this would be a way around it,
  not a shortcut.
- Read coordinator follow-ups with the preamble's `check` command at each
  natural checkpoint (before starting a new file, after a test run) and once
  more right before `worker_done`; apply a follow-up at a clean point. Run
  the verification this repository requires before
  reporting done. Do not edit a file another active task worktree has
  declared in its scope.
<!-- orca-worktree-rules:end -->

## Orca Pod fork rules

This repository is a personal fork of stablyai/orca (base branch `orcapod`, cut from tag `v1.4.268`).
The work adds an `island` home tab to the mobile app. The plan lives at
`/Users/mbp16-max/app-develop/orcabots-ios/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-22-orca-mobile-island-tab.md`.

- Also read and follow `AGENTS.md` at the repository root; it holds the upstream repository's own rules.
- Keep the diff against upstream small: put new code under `mobile/src/island/` and
  `mobile/scripts/build-island-webview-engine.mjs`. Do not change `mobile/package.json`, any lockfile,
  or `mobile/src/i18n/locales/*.json`.
- Files that two task worktrees must never edit at the same time:
  `mobile/src/home/MobileHomeScreen.tsx`, `mobile/src/home/tabs/home-tabs.ts`,
  `mobile/src/home/tabs/MobileHomeTabBar.tsx`, `mobile/app.json`, `mobile/src/island/island-types.ts`.
- Heavy commands (run only through the `orca-heavy.sh run --` wrapper the Dispatch names):
  `pnpm install`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm native ensure ios`.
- Verification before reporting done (from `mobile/`):
  1. `pnpm vitest run src/island`
  2. `pnpm lint`
  3. `pnpm typecheck` (heavy)
- iOS only. Android-specific work is out of scope.
